results.title: Partial-correctness Hoare triple for PDL programs
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Partial correctness as inclusion in the relational core

results.title: Hoare triples as KAT test inequalities

results.title: Hoare triples as KAT absorption equations

results.title: Hoare triples with formula assertions as box validity
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Hoare rule of consequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Strengthen the precondition and weaken the postcondition.

results.title: Hoare rule for sequential composition
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Hoare rule for nondeterministic choice
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Hoare rule for formula tests
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A formula test requires the postcondition only where the test passes.

results.title: Hoare invariant rule for iteration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A one-step invariant holds after every finite number of iterations, including zero, via CSLib's canonical closure-preservation theorem.

results.title: Guarded while loop in PDL
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A guarded loop in the existing PDL syntax: iterate guarded body steps, then test that the guard is false.

results.title: Hoare invariant rule for guarded while loops
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The guarded-loop invariant rule is partial correctness, including zero-step exits; it does not guarantee termination.

results.title: While-loop rule with initialization and exit implication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Verify a guarded loop using initialization, invariant preservation, and the exit implication to the desired postcondition.

results.title: Semantic completeness of the while-loop invariant rule
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The guarded-loop rule is semantically complete for arbitrary set assertions. The witness is guarded-body reachability from `P`, independent of `Q`; this is not a completeness claim for a syntactic assertion language.

results.title: PDL induction restricted to reachable states
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: PDL induction restricted to states reachable from the initial world. This proves `[a*](φ → [a]φ) → (φ → [a*]φ)` without assuming preservation on unreachable states.

results.title: Test absorption lifts through iteration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Concrete relational test absorption lifts through PDL iteration, connecting the algebraic verification equation to closure invariance.

results.title: Loop exit absorption from a guarded-body absorption equation

results.summary: A guarded-body verification equation implies the loop's exit verification equation over the same canonical relational carrier.

results.title: Prefix sum of a finite real sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real numbers $\lambda_0, \dots, \lambda_{n-1}$ and a natural number $k \le n$, the prefix sum of length $k$ is $\sum_{i < k} \lambda_i$, the sum of the first $k$ entries. Applied to the eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix, listed in decreasing order, it is the sum of the $k$ largest ones.

results.title: Ky Fan inequality for sums of largest eigenvalues
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be Hermitian $n \times n$ complex matrices and let $k \le n$. Then the sum of the $k$ largest eigenvalues of $A + B$ is at most the sum of the $k$ largest eigenvalues of $A$ plus the sum of the $k$ largest eigenvalues of $B$, where eigenvalues are counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Normalized univalent functions (the class $S$)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is in the class $S$ when it is analytic on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$, satisfies $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$, and is injective on $\mathbb{D}$.

results.title: Starlike functions on the unit disc
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is starlike when it is analytic on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$ and, for every $z \ne 0$ in $\mathbb{D}$, $f(z) \ne 0$ and $\operatorname{Re}\bigl(z f'(z) / f(z)\bigr) > 0$.

results.title: Hayman's successive coefficient problem for starlike functions

results.title: Leung's theorem on successive coefficients of starlike functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$, with $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$, injective on $\mathbb{D}$, and starlike, meaning that $\operatorname{Re}\bigl(z f'(z) / f(z)\bigr) > 0$ for every $z \ne 0$ in $\mathbb{D}$. Let $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ be the Taylor coefficients of $f$ at $0$. Then $\bigl| |a_{n+1}| - |a_n| \bigr| \le 1$ for every natural number…

results.title: One-parameter group of complex matrices
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For $m \in \mathbb{N}$, a map $\varphi \colon \mathbb{R} \to M_m(\mathbb{C})$ into the complex $m \times m$ matrices is a one-parameter group when $\varphi(0)$ is the identity matrix $I$, $\varphi(s + t) = \varphi(s)\,\varphi(t)$ for all real $s$ and $t$, and $\varphi$ is differentiable.

results.title: One-parameter group in a subgroup of the general linear group
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $G$ be a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb{C})$. A map $\varphi \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb{C})$ is a one-parameter group in $G$ when the matrix-valued map $t \mapsto \varphi(t)$ is a one-parameter group and $\varphi(t) \in G$ for every real $t$.

results.title: The lift of a one-parameter group to the general linear group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\varphi \colon \mathbb{R} \to M_m(\mathbb{C})$ be a one-parameter group of complex $m \times m$ matrices. For every real $t$ the matrix $\varphi(t)$ is invertible with inverse $\varphi(-t)$; this gives the element of $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb{C})$ with matrix $\varphi(t)$ and inverse $\varphi(-t)$.

results.title: Underlying matrix of the lift of a one-parameter group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\varphi \colon \mathbb{R} \to M_m(\mathbb{C})$ be a one-parameter group of complex $m \times m$ matrices. For every real $t$, the element of $\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb{C})$ assigned to $t$ by the lift of $\varphi$ has underlying matrix $\varphi(t)$.

results.title: One-parameter groups of matrices are exponentials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$. If $\varphi \colon \mathbb{R} \to M_m(\mathbb{C})$ is a one-parameter group of complex $m \times m$ matrices, then there is a unique matrix $A \in M_m(\mathbb{C})$ such that $\varphi(t) = \exp(tA)$ for every real $t$.

results.title: Exponential curves are one-parameter groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and every complex $m \times m$ matrix $A$, the map $t \mapsto \exp(tA)$ from $\mathbb{R}$ to the complex $m \times m$ matrices is a one-parameter group.

results.title: Detailed balance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The row vector `π` is in detailed balance with the matrix `Q`: `π i * Q i j = π j * Q j i` for all `i j` (Norris 1997, §3.7). This is only the algebraic equation: it holds for `π = 0` and every `Q`. For a probability vector `π` and a stochastic matrix it is the reversibility of the chain started from `π`.

results.title: Invariance under the semigroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `π Q = 0` if and only if `π P t = π` for every real `t` (Norris 1997, §3.5, finite state space).

results.title: Detailed balance implies invariance for the generator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Detailed balance with a matrix whose rows sum to `0` implies invariance `π Q = 0` (Norris 1997, §3.7).

results.title: Detailed balance propagates to the transition function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Detailed balance for `Q` implies `π i P t i j = π j P t j i` for every `t` (Norris 1997, §3.7). For a probability vector `π` and a rate matrix `Q` this is the reversibility of the chain started from `π`.

results.title: Detailed balance implies invariance for the transition semigroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Detailed balance with a matrix whose rows sum to `0` (for instance a rate matrix) makes `π` invariant for every `P t`.

part.title: Functional dependencies
api: A functional dependency holds in a relation
One round of the attribute-closure algorithm

results.title: Functional dependency
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A functional dependency $X \to Y$ over a type $A$ of attributes consists of two finite sets of attributes $X, Y \subseteq A$: the determining attributes $X$ (its left side) and the determined attributes $Y$ (its right side).

results.title: A functional dependency holds in a relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a type of attributes and $V$ a type of values. A functional dependency $X \to Y$ on $A$ holds in a relation $r$, a set of tuples $A \to V$, when any two tuples $t, u \in r$ that agree on every attribute of $X$ also agree on every attribute of $Y$.

results.title: A relation satisfies a set of dependencies
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over attributes $A$, and let $r$ be a relation, given as a set of tuples $A \to V$ with values in a type $V$. Then $r$ satisfies $F$ when every dependency of $F$ holds in $r$.

results.title: Entailment of functional dependencies
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a type of attributes. A finite set $F$ of functional dependencies on $A$ entails a functional dependency $f$ on $A$ when, for every type $V$ and every relation $r$ with values in $V$ (a set of tuples $A \to V$) that satisfies $F$, the dependency $f$ holds in $r$.

results.title: Derivability with Armstrong's axioms
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a set $A$ of attributes. Derivability from $F$ is the least property of functional dependencies over $A$ such that, for all finite sets $X$, $Y$, $Z$ of attributes: every dependency of $F$ is derivable; $X \to Y$ is derivable whenever $Y \subseteq X$ (reflexivity); if $X \to Y$ is derivable, then so is $X \cup Z \to Y \cup Z$ (augmentation); and if $X \to Y$…

results.title: Armstrong's axioms are sound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A derivable dependency holds in every relation satisfying `F`.

results.title: Decomposition rule
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X$, $Y$, $Z$ finite sets of attributes with $Z \subseteq Y$. If $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to Z$.

results.title: Union rule
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y, Z$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ and $X \to Z$ are derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to Y \cup Z$.

results.title: Pseudotransitivity rule
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y, W, Z$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ and $Y \cup W \to Z$ are derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \cup W \to Z$.

results.title: Adding the left side to the right side
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to X \cup Y$.

results.title: One round of the attribute-closure algorithm
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $F$ of functional dependencies and a finite set $Y$ of attributes, one closure round returns $Y$ together with the right side of every dependency of $F$ whose left side is contained in $Y$, that is, the set $Y \cup \bigcup \{R : (L \to R) \in F,\ L \subseteq Y\}$.

results.title: Iterated closure rounds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies, $n$ a natural number and $Y$ a finite set of attributes. The loop returns $Y$ if $n = 0$ or if one closure round for $F$ leaves $Y$ unchanged; otherwise it returns the loop with $n - 1$ rounds started from the result of one closure round applied to $Y$. Thus it repeats closure rounds from $Y$ until nothing changes, for at most $n$ rounds.

results.title: Attribute closure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. The attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$ is computed by the closure algorithm: starting from $X$, repeat closure rounds (each adds the right side of every dependency of $F$ whose left side is already included) until nothing changes, for at most $|A|$ rounds.

results.title: The attribute closure is a fixed point of a closure round
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. Applying one closure round for $F$ to the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$ returns $X^+$.

results.title: The attribute closure is closed under the dependencies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes, $X$ a set of attributes and $X^+$ its attribute closure under $F$. For every dependency $Y \to Z$ in $F$ with $Y \subseteq X^+$, also $Z \subseteq X^+$.

results.title: Closure witness relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. The closure witness relation for $X$ is the relation with values in $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ whose tuples are the tuple that is $\mathrm{true}$ on every attribute and the tuple that is $\mathrm{true}$ exactly on the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$. These two tuples agree exactly on…

results.title: The closure witness satisfies the dependencies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. For every set $X \subseteq A$ of attributes, the closure witness relation for $X$ under $F$ satisfies $F$.

results.title: The closure algorithm decides derivability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X, Y \subseteq A$. Then $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms if and only if $Y \subseteq X^+$, where $X^+$ is the attribute closure of $X$ under $F$ computed by the closure algorithm.

results.title: The closure algorithm computes the attribute closure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes and $X$ a set of attributes. An attribute $a$ lies in the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$, as computed by the closure algorithm, if and only if the dependency $X \to \{a\}$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms.

results.title: Completeness of Armstrong's axioms, two-tuple form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $f$ a functional dependency over $A$. If $f$ holds in every relation with values in $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that has at most two tuples and satisfies every dependency of $F$, then $f$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms.

results.title: Armstrong's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $f$ a functional dependency over $A$. Then $f$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms if and only if $F$ entails $f$, that is, $f$ holds in every relation (with values in any type) that satisfies every dependency of $F$. In other words, Armstrong's axioms are sound and complete for functional dependencies.

results.title: Superkey
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes $A$. A set of attributes $K$ is a superkey for $F$ when the dependency $K \to A$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, that is, $K$ determines every attribute.

results.title: Candidate key
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. A set $K \subseteq A$ of attributes is a candidate key for $F$ when $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and no proper subset of $K$ is a superkey for $F$.

results.title: Supersets of superkeys are superkeys
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes. If $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and $K \subseteq K'$, then $K'$ is a superkey for $F$.

results.title: Tuples that agree on a superkey are equal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $K$ be a superkey for $F$. Let $V$ be a type of values. If a relation $r$, a set of tuples $A \to V$, satisfies $F$, then any two tuples $t, u \in r$ that agree on every attribute of $K$ are equal.

results.title: Candidate keys are the superkeys minimal under single removals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. A set $K \subseteq A$ of attributes is a candidate key for $F$ if and only if $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and, for every $a \in K$, the set $K \setminus \{a\}$ is not a superkey for $F$.

results.title: Shrinking a key along a list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes. Given a list $l$ of attributes and a set of attributes $K$, go through $l$ in order and, for each attribute $a$, remove $a$ from the current set whenever the attribute closure under $F$ of the current set without $a$ is the set of all attributes (that is, the set without $a$ is still a superkey); the result is the set reached at the…

results.title: Key-finding algorithm
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $l$ be a list of attributes. The key-finding algorithm starts from the set $K = A$ of all attributes and goes through $l$ in order: for each listed attribute $a$, it replaces $K$ by $K \setminus \{a\}$ when the attribute closure of $K \setminus \{a\}$ under $F$ is all of $A$, and keeps $K$ otherwise. It returns the final…

results.title: The key-finding algorithm returns a candidate key
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $l$ be a list in which every attribute of $A$ occurs. Then the output of the key-finding algorithm on $F$ and $l$, which starts from the set of all attributes and goes through $l$ in order, removing each listed attribute whenever what remains is still a superkey, is a candidate key for $F$.

results.title: Every superkey contains a candidate key
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. Every superkey $K$ for $F$ has a subset $K' \subseteq K$ that is a candidate key for $F$.

results.summary: The random-cluster connection probability `φ_{G,p,q}(x ↔ y)`.

results.title: Functions equal at two points as functions omitting one point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For `a ≠ b`, functions `C → Fin q` with `f a = f b` correspond to functions on `C \ {b}`.

results.title: Correspondence for cluster-constant colorings equal at two vertices
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Colorings constant on open clusters with `σ x = σ y` correspond to colorings of the clusters that agree on the clusters of `x` and `y`.

results.title: Ising two-point function from the Edwards–Sokal coupling
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Ising two-point function `⟨σ_x σ_y⟩` at bond parameter `p`, computed as the Edwards–Sokal spin marginal.

results.title: Ising two-point function equals the $q = 2$ connection probability
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The Ising two-point function equals the random-cluster connection probability with `q = 2`: `⟨σ_x σ_y⟩ = φ_{p,2}(x ↔ y)` (Edwards–Sokal 1988; Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model*, 2006, Theorem 1.16).
